newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI revises valuation norms for new Indian banks.
newsitem.headline: RBI revises valuation norms for new Indian banks.

text.p: New private sector Indian banks will be required to mark to market all their investments in approved securities at the end of March 1997 and thereafter, bankers said on Wednesday.
Earlier the banks were allowed to classify a maximum of 50 percent of such investments as "permanent" and did not need to provide for depreciation in their market value.

"On a review, it has been decided that the new banks in the private sector.....should mark to market their entire investments in governemnt securities as at the end of March 1997 and thereafter," the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in a circular.

The rule would apply to those banks which had been set up after April 1, 1994 pursuant to the RBI guidelines dated January 22, 1993 and the issue of licences under section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the RBI circular said.
